title: We will form next govt in Haryana, claims Hooda
text: Leader of the opposition in Haryana assembly Bhupinder Singh Hooda Mahendragarh: Former Haryana chief minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Monday alleged that the BJP formed the govt in Haryana through âvote theftâ rather than through a genuine electoral mandate, and claimed that subsequent investigations had raised serious questions about the conduct of the 2024 Assembly elections. Addressing a Congress workersâ conference of the Mahendragarh Block Congress at Satnali, Hooda alleged that evidence supporting the partyâs concerns had now emerged. Referring to Rahul Gandhi âs earlier allegations, he claimed that media reports had also raised questions about the Election Commission âs functioning and its alleged proximity to the ruling BJP. Hooda said Congress workers and voters across communities had expected the party to return to power in the 2024 Assembly elections. âEveryone was saying that the BJP was on its way out and the Congress was coming to power, yet the results turned out to be exactly the opposite,â he said. He claimed that he had expressed doubts about the election results immediately after the polls and said a subsequent investigation by Rahul Gandhi and the Congress had, according to the party, brought the issue of alleged electoral irregularities into focus. Hooda also questioned the changes in Haryanaâs voter turnout figures released after polling. According to him, the Election Commission initially reported voter turnout at 61.19% on the night of Oct 5, 2024, but the figure was subsequently revised to 65.65% the following day and 67.9% on October 7, shortly before counting. âIt is incomprehensible how the vote count increased so significantly after the EVMs had been sealed,â Hooda said, while demanding answers from the Election Commission. He alleged that the Congress had raised several questions with the poll panel following the election but had not received satisfactory answers. Calling upon Congress workers to strengthen the party organisation at the grassroots level, Hooda praised senior Congress leader Rao Dan Singh, and said the next government in Haryana would be formed by the Congress. He urged party workers to strengthen Rao Dan Singhâs leadership in the region, saying this would help address local issues and accelerate development. He additionally claimed that the stateâs economic position had deteriorated, alleging that Haryana had slipped to the 14th position among 18 major states. title: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 cr of 12.10 cr
text: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 crore NEW DELHI: The Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party received Rs 12.10 crore in contributions in 2025-26, a 68% drop from the previous financial year, according to its latest report filed with the Election Commission. Nearly 83% of the party's contributions came from two donors, Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited. Both gave Rs 5 crore each. Trident was founded by former AAP Rajya Sabha member Rajinder Gupta. The remaining contributions amounted to around Rs 2.10 crore, according to the report. Gupta was elected to the Rajya Sabha on an AAP ticket in October 2025. Trident's Rs 5-crore cheque was dated January 9, 2026, when Gupta was still with the AAP. He joined the BJP after Raghav Chadha led rebellion, merging two-third of AAP's Rajya Sabha strength into the ruling saffron party in April this year. The AAP had reported contributions of Rs 38.10 crore in 2024-25, compared with Rs 11.06 crore in 2023-24. Prudent Electoral Trust was the party's biggest donor that year, contributing Rs 16.40 crore. The latest filing covers the first full financial year after the AAP lost power in Delhi in February 2025. The party continues to govern Punjab, where Trident is based. The AAP report has 1,202 numbered entries. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora is listed against 12 payments of Rs 10,000 each, adding up to Rs 1.20 lakh. How other regional parties fared The latest filings of other regional parties also show a decline in contributions compared with 2024-25. The Telugu Desam Party (TDP), which came to power in Andhra Pradesh, reported Rs 58.25 crore in contributions in 2025-26, down from Rs 83.03 crore the previous year. Prudent Electoral Trust was its biggest donor, giving Rs 45 crore, compared with Rs 40 crore in 2024-25. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which lost power in Andhra Pradesh to the TDP, reported contributions of Rs 24.31 crore. This was sharply lower than the Rs 140.04 crore it reported in 2024-25. Its biggest donor in the latest filing was Goodwood Sanctuary Private Limited, which contributed Rs 10 crore. title: Congress resets Team Uttar Pradesh: 5 clear messages for BJP and Akhilesh Yadav
text: Congress replaced Ajay Rai with Aradhana Misra Mona as Uttar Pradesh Congress chief. NEW DELHI: Congress has overhauled its Uttar Pradesh organisation ahead of the 2027 assembly election, replacing Ajay Rai with three-time Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as state unit president and appointing Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president. The party has also named Chaudhary Virendra Singh as Congress legislature party leader. The reshuffle brings together a prominent Brahmin leader from eastern UP, a Muslim leader with influence in western UP, and Dalit and OBC representation in senior organisational positions. Rajendra Pal Gautam, a Dalit leader, is already the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge. With these recent appointments, Congress may be trying to widen its social and regional reach after years of electoral decline in the state. Taken together, the appointments suggest that Congress is trying to do two things at once: strengthen its bargaining position with the Samajwadi Party while rebuilding an independent political identity in Uttar Pradesh. The timing is important. The 2024 Lok Sabha election revived Congress's presence in UP through its alliance with Akhilesh Yadav . But Akhileshâs party remains the much larger organisation in the state. In the 2024 polls, SP moved 32 seats up and won 37 seats, registering a 15.73% gain in vote share. On the other hand, Congress also slightly improved its Lok Sabha tally with 6 seats and a jump of a little over 3% vote share. Congress is now trying to turn that electoral revival into a more substantial organisational base before the 2027 assembly election in a state which has been long associated with Congress's political success story. Here are the five messages embedded in the reset. 1. A bigger, but amicable, say at seat-sharing table The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona as UPCC president, along with the elevation of Imran Masood, suggests that Congress wants to push for a larger share of assembly seats while keeping its relationship with the Samajwadi Party workable. What Mona Misra said after her appointment as UP Congress chief Masood has been unusually vocal about Congress' seat demand. On September 3, he argued that if Congress' electoral performance continued to improve, its share of seats should also increase. "Hum koi bhikhari hain jo Samajwadi Party se bheekh mangenge? ... Party formula tay karegi, lekin jo formula Lok Sabha election mein tha, woh formula nahi hoga. (Are we beggars who will beg from Samajwadi Party? ... The party will decide the formula, but it will not be the same formula used in the Lok Sabha elections)," he had told ANI. Congress' UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has also spoken of seeking an equal number of seats with the SP, while Masood has backed a 50:50 formula. The rhetoric sharpened on September 28, when Masood directly declared: "If Akhilesh Yadav is unhappy (with seat-sharing discussion), the loss will be his own... We fail to understand what the anger is even about." Mona's elevation, on the other hand, sends a somewhat different signal. Unlike the more combative rhetoric around seat-sharing, her appointment gives Congress a state president who is seen as having a more workable equation with the SP leadership. Her political experience and close association with the Congress leadership also give her a role in managing the alliance even as the party pushes for greater space. The numbers give Congress some basis for making that argument. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP won 37 of UP's 80 seats while Congress won six, taking the INDIA bloc's combined tally to 43. The SP's 37-seat tally was a dramatic rise from five seats in 2019. However, going by the numbers, Congress cannot negotiate from the position of higher power and will most likely have to settle for the junior partner role. But how "small" the partner role it gets will be crucial. 2. Rebuilding old social reach, but with a new mix One of the clearest messages in the new team is social and regional balancing. Mona is a prominent Brahmin face from eastern Uttar Pradesh. Masood brings a prominent Muslim face from western UP. Devinder Nishad gives the organisation an OBC, riverine-community face, while Alok Prasad brings Dalit representation into the senior state team. Rajendra Pal Gautam is already the party's Dalit in-charge for Uttar Pradesh. The choice of Mona is particularly significant because she replaces Ajay Rai, a Bhumihar leader, with another upper-caste leader from a different community. The switch from Rai to Mona could be read as an attempt to reconnect with Brahmin voters who were traditionally associated with Congress but have, over time, moved substantially towards the BJP. What Ajay Rai said after being replaced as UP Congress chief This rejig comes at a time when the upper-caste groups (Rajputs, Brahmins, Tyagis) reportedly feel increasingly sidelined by BJP's aggressive outreach toward non-Yadav OBC and Dalit vote banks. Tensions stem from ticket distribution cuts, perceived administrative favour toward Rajputs over Brahmins, and farmers' issues. Mona's appointment, however, is not simply a return to Congress's old social formula. The new team combines upper-caste, Muslim, Dalit and OBC representation, while also distributing the leadership geographically between eastern and western UP. The BJP has built a broad social coalition of its own in Uttar Pradesh. Congress' organisational response now appears to be an attempt to create multiple social entry points into the party rather than rely on a single caste or community bloc. 3. Not conceding Muslim vote Masood's elevation carries another particularly important message for western Uttar Pradesh. The Saharanpur MP is one of Congress' most prominent Muslim leaders in the state, and his appointment puts a western UP Muslim face in the second-most important position in the state organisation. His appointment seems to be a direct attempt to attract and consolidate Muslim support. That matters because the SP has traditionally been the principal opposition party competing for the Muslim vote in UP. The 2024 Lok Sabha election demonstrated the strength of that relationship. What Imran Masood said after UP Congress organizational reshuffle A post-election CSDS-Lokniti analysis estimated that 77% of Muslim respondents in Uttar Pradesh voted for the SP and 15% for Congress, while 2% reported voting for the BJP. These are, of course, survey estimates and not absolute vote counts. However, it may reflect the trend. The actual election results also showed the importance of Muslim-heavy constituencies to the opposition's performance. Congress won Saharanpur and Sitapur, while the SP and its allies captured several other such seats. Masood's promotion therefore gives Congress a prominent vehicle to seek Muslim support directly rather than relying entirely on the SP to bring that constituency into the alliance. 4. Congress wants credibility Mona's appointment is significant because she brings an electoral record to the top of the state unit. She first entered the Uttar Pradesh assembly through a bypoll in 2014 and subsequently retained Rampur Khas in the 2017 and 2022 elections. She has therefore won the seat three times. Before entering the assembly, she served as block pramukh of Sangramgarh from 2002 to 2014 and held positions in the organisation and cooperative sector. Her 2022 victory was particularly notable because Congress was reduced to just two assembly seats across Uttar Pradesh. She defeated BJP's Nagesh Pratap Singh by 14,741 votes, polling 84,334 votes, or 50.27%, according to Election Commission data. That gives Congress a state president who is not merely an organisational appointee but an incumbent with a repeated assembly-winning record. 5. Women power at heart The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona also gives Congress a prominent woman at the helm of its Uttar Pradesh organisation, at a time when BJP too is putting renewed emphasis on its women leaders in the state. The timing is notable. The BJP has recently brought back Smriti Irani into a more prominent organisational role, signalling that women leaders continue to have an important place in its political strategy. Irani, who beat Rahul Gandhi and represented Amethi in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2024, remains one of the BJP's most recognisable women faces in Uttar Pradesh. The Mona-Priyanka Gandhi combination will give Congress a big women power picture it can easily put on its posters. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the Election Commission recorded female voter turnout in Uttar Pradesh at 57.22%, compared with 56.46% among men. Women therefore turned out at a slightly higher rate than men in the state. As a bonus, Mona's elevation also gives Congress a combination of representation and political substance: a woman leader, a Brahmin face, a three-time assembly winner and someone with an established organisational network. The new UP team combines experience with caste, community, regional and gender representation, giving Congress multiple entry points in the voter base. The real test now will be whether the reshuffle can translate into stronger grassroots organisation and enough bargaining power ahead of the 2027 assembly election. title: 2 Indians charged in US for smuggling fake Ozempic from China
text: Swapnadip Roy and Vicky Ramancha charged in US for smuggling fake Ozempic from China. Two Indian nationals have been charged in the United States for allegedly smuggling counterfeit Ozempic, a weight-loss drug, from China and selling the products to distributors in the country, the Department of Justice said Tuesday. Swapnadip Roy, 33, and Vicky Ramancha, 37, were charged in the Middle District of Florida. Roy was extradited from Italy to the US and made his initial appearance in Tampa on Tuesday, where he pleaded not guilty. Ramancha remains at large. Prosecutors allege that Roy and Ramancha obtained counterfeit Ozempic in China between July 2023 and April 2024 and sold the products to US distributors at discounted prices. The counterfeit products allegedly included packaging, package inserts, pen labels and needles designed to make buyers believe they were purchasing genuine Ozempic authorised by the manufacturer. The alleged scheme continued even after the US Food and Drug Administration seized some of the counterfeit Ozempic in December 2023 and issued a public warning about the products, the department said. Roy and Ramancha are charged with one count of conspiracy to commit smuggling and defraud the United States, three counts of smuggling, and two counts of selling counterfeit drugs and holding counterfeit drugs for sale. If convicted, each faces a maximum sentence of 71 years in prison. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department's Criminal Division said counterfeit prescription drugs pose a threat to people who depend on the safety of the pharmaceutical supply. âThese defendants allegedly exploited peopleâs health to pay themselves. We will keep pursuing anyone who seeks to deceive American consumers with counterfeit drugs,â Duva said. Assistant US Attorney Christopher Murray for the Middle District of Florida said the indictment reflected the department's efforts to protect Americans from potential harm caused by counterfeit prescription drugs. The FDA's Office of Criminal Investigations is investigating the case. Assistant Commissioner Justin Green said introducing counterfeit drugs into the US pharmaceutical supply chain puts consumers at significant risk. Roy was arrested in Italy pursuant to an INTERPOL Red Notice before the Justice Department secured his continued detention and sought his extradition to the US. You use AI every day. title: Indian green card holder charged in Texas over illegal voting crackdown; 6 others also booked
text: Khalwinder Singh Bhengura was arrested on September 11 in US. A 69-year-old Indian Green Card holder is among seven non-citizens facing federal charges in Texas over alleged illegal voting or false claims of US citizenship. Khalwinder Singh Bhengura, an Indian man and lawful permanent resident since 2022, has been charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and making a false statement of citizenship to register to vote, according to the US Attorneyâs Office for the Northern District of Texas. Prosecutors allege Bhengura claimed to be a US citizen when registering to vote in January 2024. He allegedly made another citizenship claim while applying for a Texas driver's licence in August that year and later voted in the November 2024 general election. Authorities said Bhengura subsequently admitted that he knew he was not a US citizen. He was arrested on September 11. Bhengura is one of seven non-citizens charged as part of a federal investigation into voting and citizenship-related offences in North Texas. Six defendants were indicted on September 10, while another was charged through a criminal complaint the following day. Federal authorities said the arrests followed the charges. The other defendants include Nigerian nationals Helen Mayen Adams and Joshua Nmelichukwu Akpom, Mexican nationals Carlos Salas Barrios, Rocio Thrasher and Moises Anwar Arellano-Alba, and Celestin Katubadi, a citizen of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The cases differ. Prosecutors allege Adams, Barrios, Thrasher, Katubadi and Arellano-Alba were involved in voting-related offences or false claims of citizenship. Akpom faces a separate charge involving alleged false statements in a naturalisation application regarding previous claims of US citizenship, voter registration, and voting. In Bhenguraâs case, prosecutors allege the ballot was cast in Tarrant County during the November 2024 election. The federal case is being investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the FBI Dallas field office, with assistance from the Texas Attorney Generalâs Election Integrity Unit and the Tarrant County District Attorneyâs Office. US Attorney Ryan Raybould said federal authorities would pursue cases involving non-citizens who vote in federal elections or falsely claim citizenship. âFederal elections belong to American citizensâperiod,â Raybould said, adding that the charges were intended to enforce federal election laws. HSI Dallas acting Deputy Special Agent in Charge Judy Pardo described election integrity as a national security priority, while FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock said the bureau would investigate allegations of voter fraud and other election crimes. The charges concern alleged conduct during the 2024 election cycle.
